in_scope_details.question: Which network function terminates the NAS signalling coming from the UE?
in_scope_details.answer: The Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) terminates the NAS signalling coming from the UE. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.1 (Network functions overview), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which function is in charge of forwarding user data in the 5G Core?
in_scope_details.answer: The User Plane Function (UPF) is responsible for forwarding user data in the 5G Core. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.1 (Network functions overview), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Through what kind of architecture do the 5G Core network functions interact with each other?
in_scope_details.answer: The 5G Core network functions interact with each other through a service-based architecture. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.1 (Network functions overview), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which network function supplies QoS and charging-related policy rules to the AMF and SMF?
in_scope_details.answer: The Policy Control Function (PCF) supplies QoS and charging-related policy rules to the AMF and SMF. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.3 (Policy and data management functions), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which function stores subscription data in the 5G Core?
in_scope_details.answer: I couldn't find this information in the provided 3GPP specifications.

in_scope_details.question: Which function keeps a registry of available NF instances so that they can discover each other?
in_scope_details.answer: The Network Repository Function (NRF) keeps a registry of available NF instances so that they can discover each other. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.3 (Policy and data management functions), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: With which function does the UDM cooperate to generate authentication credentials?
in_scope_details.answer: The UDM cooperates with the Authentication Server Function (AUSF) to generate authentication credentials. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 4.2.3 (Policy and data management functions), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: How many network slices can serve a UE at the same time through one registration?
in_scope_details.answer: A UE may be simultaneously served by up to eight Network Slices via a single registration. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 5.15.3 (Network slicing), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Is the Slice Differentiator a mandatory part of the S-NSSAI?
in_scope_details.answer: I couldn't find this information in the provided 3GPP specifications.

in_scope_details.question: What identifier is used to identify a Network Slice?
in_scope_details.answer: The identifier used to identify a Network Slice is the Single Network Slice Selection Assistance Information (S-NSSAI), which consists of a Slice/Service Type (SST) and an optional Slice Differentiator (SD). [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 5.15.3 (Network slicing), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which slice/service type has the standardized SST value 1?
in_scope_details.answer: The standardized SST value 1 corresponds to the eMBB slice/service type. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 5.15.4 (Standardized SST values), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What SST value is assigned to Massive IoT?
in_scope_details.answer: The SST value assigned to Massive IoT is 3. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: Which standardized SST value is used for vehicle-to-everything communications?
in_scope_details.answer: The standardized SST value used for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications is 4. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: In which registration management state does the AMF hold no valid location or routing information for the UE?
in_scope_details.answer: The AMF holds no valid location or routing information for the UE when the UE is in the RM-DEREGISTERED state. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 8.2.1 (Registration management states), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: In which registration management state can the network reach the UE for paging?
in_scope_details.answer: The network can reach the UE for paging when the UE is in the RM-REGISTERED registration management state. [TS 23.501 v17.9.0, Clause 8.2.1 (Registration management states), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: For which purposes does a UE use the registration procedure?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE uses the registration procedure for initial registration, mobility registration update, periodic registration update, or emergency registration. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.1.3 (Registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which message does the AMF send back when it accepts a registration?
in_scope_details.answer: The AMF sends a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.1.3 (Registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Under what condition does the UE acknowledge with REGISTRATION COMPLETE?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE acknowledges with REGISTRATION COMPLETE if new 5G-GUTI or TAI list values were assigned. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.1.3 (Registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which sides are able to initiate de-registration?
in_scope_details.answer: Both the UE and the network can initiate de-registration. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.5.1 (De-registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What does the UE indicate in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST that it sends?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE indicates whether it wishes to switch off. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.5.1 (De-registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: How should the UE reply to a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST sent by the AMF?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE shall reply with a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message, unless the switch-off indicator in the request makes an acknowledgement unnecessary. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.5.1 (De-registration procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which NAS timer supervises the de-registration procedure?
in_scope_details.answer: Timer T3521 supervises the de-registration procedure. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 10.2 (NAS timers), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What is the default value of timer T3511?
in_scope_details.answer: The default value of timer T3511 is 10 seconds [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What is the retransmission limit associated with timer T3510?
in_scope_details.answer: The retransmission limit associated with timer T3510 is 5 attempts [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What does the UE do if T3510 expires before it receives a response from the network?
in_scope_details.answer: I couldn't find this information in the provided 3GPP specifications.

in_scope_details.question: Which NAS message carries the authentication challenge to the UE?
in_scope_details.answer: I couldn't find this information in the provided 3GPP specifications.

in_scope_details.question: What does the UE use to calculate its authentication response?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE calculates its authentication response using its USIM. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.4.1 (Authentication procedure), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: After an AUTHENTICATION REJECT, until when does the UE treat the USIM as invalid for 5GS services?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE shall consider the USIM invalid for 5GS services until the UE is switched off or the USIM is removed. [TS 24.501 v17.8.0, Clause 5.4.1 (Authentication procedure), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: From which function does the AUSF request authentication vectors in 5G-AKA?
in_scope_details.answer: The AUSF requests authentication vectors from the UDM. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 0 (Front matter), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Where are the subscriber-specific keys used to derive authentication vectors stored?
in_scope_details.answer: The subscriber-specific keys used to derive authentication vectors are stored in the ARPF. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 0 (Front matter), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which shared anchor key do the UE and the network derive after a successful 5G-AKA run?
in_scope_details.answer: They derive the shared anchor key K_SEAF. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 0 (Front matter), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which entity forwards the authentication challenge to the UE and verifies its response?
in_scope_details.answer: The SEAF forwards the authentication challenge to the UE via the AMF and verifies the UE's response before considering the subscriber authenticated. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 0 (Front matter), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which key sits at the root of the 5G key hierarchy?
in_scope_details.answer: The root of the 5G key hierarchy is the long-term subscriber key K. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 6.2.1 (Key hierarchy), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: From which key does the AMF derive K_AMF?
in_scope_details.answer: The AMF derives K_AMF from K_SEAF. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 6.2.1 (Key hierarchy), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What is the parent key of K_gNB?
in_scope_details.answer: The parent key of K_gNB is K_AMF. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 6.2.2 (Key derivation summary), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: Which entities derive the key K_AUSF?
in_scope_details.answer: The key K_AUSF is derived by the Authentication Server Function (AUSF) and the UE from the long-term subscriber key K. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 6.2.2 (Key derivation summary), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: Which NAS and Access Stratum keys are derived from K_AMF for a given registration?
in_scope_details.answer: The NAS and Access Stratum keys that are derived from K_AMF for a given registration are: - K_NASint - K_NASenc - K_gNB These keys are derived from K_AMF as stated in the key hierarchy description. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 6.2.1 (Key hierarchy), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: For what reason may user plane integrity protection be disabled?
in_scope_details.answer: User plane integrity protection may be disabled when the data rate exceeds a maximum data rate configured by the network, for performance reasons. [TS 33.501 v17.7.0, Clause 5.9.2 (User plane integrity protection), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What are the four messages exchanged in the contention-based random access procedure?
in_scope_details.answer: The four messages exchanged in the contention-based random access procedure are: 1. Msg1 – Random access preamble (UE transmits) 2. Msg2 – Random access response (network grants uplink resources) 3. Msg3 – Scheduled message containing UE identity (UE transmits) 4. Msg4 – Contention resolution message (network resolves contention) [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause 5.1.2 (Random access procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What does the random access response grant to the UE?
in_scope_details.answer: The random access response (Msg2) grants the UE uplink resources. [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause 5.1.2 (Random access procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Why does the two-step random access procedure exist?
in_scope_details.answer: The two-step random access procedure exists to reduce latency by combining the preamble and Msg3 payload into a single MsgA transmission. [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause 5.1.2 (Random access procedure), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What does each HARQ process maintain on its own?
in_scope_details.answer: Each HARQ process maintains its own soft-combining buffer. [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause 5.4.2 (HARQ operation), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: How does the receiver react when it detects a transport block error?
in_scope_details.answer: The receiver shall request retransmission via HARQ feedback rather than waiting for RLC-layer retransmission, in order to minimise latency. [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause 5.4.2 (HARQ operation), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which modulation scheme is used at MCS index 27?
in_scope_details.answer: The modulation scheme used at MCS index 27 is 256QAM [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What is the modulation order for MCS index 9?
in_scope_details.answer: The modulation order for MCS index 9 is 4. [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: Which MCS index in the excerpt maps to QPSK?
in_scope_details.answer: The MCS index that maps to QPSK is 0 [TS 38.321 v17.5.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: In which RRC state does the UE keep its AS context so that it can resume the connection quickly?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE keeps its AS context in the RRC_INACTIVE state, allowing it to resume the connection with reduced signalling overhead. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 4.2.1 (RRC states), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What does a UE do while it is in RRC_IDLE?
in_scope_details.answer: In RRC_IDLE, the UE monitors paging and performs cell (re)selection but has no established RRC connection with any gNB. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 4.2.1 (RRC states), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which signalling radio bearer does the RRCSetup message configure?
in_scope_details.answer: The RRCSetup message configures Signalling Radio Bearer 1 (SRB1). [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which message from the UE completes RRC connection establishment?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE completes the RRC connection establishment by sending an RRCSetupComplete message. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: How does the network respond when it cannot admit an RRC connection request?
in_scope_details.answer: The network replies with an RRCReject message, and it may include a wait timer instructing the UE to refrain from re-attempting for a specified duration. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which failures cause the UE to start RRC connection re-establishment?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE initiates RRC connection re-establishment when it detects any of the following failures, provided it has a stored AS security context and can find a suitable cell within the re-establishment timer T311: - radio link failure - handover failure - mobility from NR failure - integrity check failure - RRC connection reconfiguration failure [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.13 (RRC connection re-establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What must the UE have stored in order to initiate RRC connection re-establishment?
in_scope_details.answer: The UE must have a stored AS security context in order to initiate RRC connection re-establishment. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.13 (RRC connection re-establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: What is the default value of timer T310?
in_scope_details.answer: The default value of timer T310 is 2000 ms. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause Table@p2 (Table), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What event starts timer T311?
in_scope_details.answer: Timer T311 is started when the UE initiates the RRC connection re-establishment procedure. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 5.3.13 (RRC connection re-establishment), p.1].

in_scope_details.question: Which messages stop timer T300 when they are received?
in_scope_details.answer: Timer T300 is stopped when the UE receives either an RRCSetup or an RRCReject message. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 6.3.2 (Timers and constants (RRC)), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: Within what range can the network configure constant N311?
in_scope_details.answer: The network can configure N311 within the range 1 to 10. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 6.3.5 (Maximum values (RRC)), p.2].

in_scope_details.question: What does the constant N311 count?
in_scope_details.answer: N311 counts the number of consecutive in-sync indications required to stop T310. [TS 38.331 v17.6.0, Clause 6.3.5 (Maximum values (RRC)), p.2].
